Save and read portable recipes and analysis records

Source: R/recipe.R
lexdiv_write.Rd

JSON preserves nested metadata and typed tables (column names, types and arrays of values), including zero-row tables and character IDs. It contains source text when saving an analysis. CSV is a scalar long metric table: document x condition x request, with list columns encoded as JSON strings. Keep the JSON record beside CSV; CSV alone is not a reproducible analysis. Existing files are never overwritten. Unknown schemas are rejected.

Usage

lexdiv_write(x, path, format = c("json", "csv"))

lexdiv_read(path)

Arguments

x

A recipe or analysis produced by lexdiv_recipe() or lexdiv_run_recipe().

path

Output or input file path.

format

"json" for a recipe/analysis or "csv" for analysis metrics.

Value

lexdiv_write() invisibly returns the output path. lexdiv_read() returns a validated recipe or analysis without recalculating document scores.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("jsonlite", quietly = TRUE)) {
  recipe <- lexdiv_recipe(lexdiv_plan(presets = character(), specs = lexdiv_spec("ttr")))
  run <- lexdiv_run_recipe(c("001" = "One small example."), recipe)
  path <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
  lexdiv_write(run, path)
  restored <- lexdiv_read(path)
  stopifnot(identical(restored$analysis$results, run$analysis$results))
  unlink(path)
}
